title: Choose the visual world for AFD360 Utilities
question: The roll assigned the Flight Progress Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Flight Progress Board
options.lineage: air-traffic-control flight progress strips in a controller's bay
options.thesis: Every turn and every Salesforce call is a strip on the controller's board: live, timestamped, handed off, never lost.
materials: printed card strips in steel holders
options.viewport: Three bays: sector list of conversations, the live transcript as wide strips (clock | callsign | mark | content) with tool steps handed down as sub-strips, and the Wire as a strip rack — blue outbound, amber inbound — stacked by time.
options.risk: The strip metaphor turns into costume if holders and brackets get decorated; it must stay a dense typographic grid, not skeuomorphism.

raised.raise: Nothing disappears, it cancels: stopped, rejected and superseded turns get a stamped mark on their strip instead of vanishing.
One saturated action color, used only on things you can press; status lives in strip color and marks, never in the action color.
One tabular monospace grammar for every clock, duration, status code and id, aligned in fixed columns.
Inside dense strips, rank comes from weight, case and reversal, not size; the one live strip gets the board's only reversed plate.
Live state is a capsule whose chip crosses to the leading edge when the session is live.

options.label: Protocol Analyzer
options.thesis: The wire is the main view; the conversation is the decoded payload of each call.
options.viewport: Top: a time-ordered capture list of every call; bottom: the selected call decoded as chat turns, tool steps and raw JSON side by side.
options.risk: Familiar developer-tool look (DevTools/Wireshark): credible to engineers, can read as intimidating to a business audience on a customer call.

options.label: Jet-Age Ticket Wallet
options.lineage: 1960s airline ticket wallets with carbon coupons
options.thesis: Each conversation is a ticket wallet; every turn is a coupon that gets validated, used, or voided.
options.viewport: A coupon book: the open leg is the current turn; used legs stack as stubs, approvals stamp APPROVED or VOID across the coupon.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: approvals and session states map to stamped coupons; loses on audience (SEs and bank execs don't read the app as travel).
options.risk: Coupon chrome can crowd dense Wire data.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1971 pocket airline timetable on a light table
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight, case and reversal on a raked rack of slides.
options.viewport: Lateral rack of raked slides with a tick rail.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the 11° rake and lateral travel fight readability on a screen-share.
options.kept: Rank by weight, case and reversal instead of size inside dense rows.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Soft cards, friendly labels, one color for what you can press.
options.viewport: Single card column with a bottom bar.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a thumb-first consumer surface undersells an engineering demo tool.
options.kept: The action color appears only on things you can press.

options.label: Data-Sublime Field
options.thesis: Black and white barcode columns of pure data.
options.viewport: Dense bar fields with strobing inversion.
options.case: Fuses poorly: strobing black fields are hostile on customer calls.
options.kept: One tabular monospace grammar for every number and id.

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.thesis: Swelling lobes of flat color divide the page.
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful geography obscures dense API state.
options.kept: A live capsule whose chip crosses sides when active.

options.label: Vertical Media Feed
options.thesis: One item owns the viewport; the next is one snap away.
options.viewport: One snap-paged item at a time.
options.case: Fuses poorly: hides the history and the wire, the two things this product exists to show.
options.kept: The next action is always loaded and waiting (composer ready the moment a turn ends).

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished AI-chat app: conversation sidebar, centered thread, inspector panel, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, centered chat thread with message bubbles, collapsible inspector on the right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every AI chat tool by design; the Wire stays a side panel.
